items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick has become one of the military’s biggest — and busiest — evangelists for AI. The GenAI Task Force travels around the globe to sit down with troops on operations floors and in the field and find AI fixes for their most pressing problems. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.”

Một thay đổi quan trọng là nhiều bài kiểm tra hiện được giữ bí mật, khiến các công ty AI khó huấn luyện mô hình dựa theo đó. Sức mạnh điện toán này thấp đáng ngạc nhiên nếu xét đến sự chú ý khổng lồ dành cho các mô hình AI Trung Quốc hiện nay. Dù vậy, một số chuyên gia lưu ý, OpenRouter chỉ đại diện cho một phần thị trường, nên số liệu này không phản ánh hết nhu cầu về mô hình trọng số mở.

items.title: ATTENTION. I wrote a guide about SEVEN things that look completely normal. A PHONE update. A screenshot. A charger. A se
items.summary:
ATTENTION. I wrote a guide about SEVEN things that look completely normal. A PHONE update. A screenshot. A charger. A sealed box. A QR sticker. A selfie. A data archive.

None of them looks like an attack. Every one has a documented case.

→ The update: Apple pays up to $2,000,000 for a spyware-grade iPhone chain, over $5,000,000 with bonuses. $35,000,000 has gone to 800+ researchers.

→ The screenshot: SparkCat read seed phrases in photo galleries. 242,000+ downloads on Google Play alone.

→ The archive: Meta paid $5 billion to the FTC in 2019 and $650 million over face scanning.

→ The money at the end of it: $713 million stolen from personal crypto wallets in 2025.

Before I wrote a single prompt, I wrote the rules. One file, CLAUDE.md, which I call Claude Core. Read only. Local only. Secrets masked to the first 2 and last 2 characters. Evidence first.

Why rules first? Because Claude Code reads what is on your devices in minutes and points at the one line that should not be there. That is the job. It must never touch, and never send.

The AI is already inside Apple’s world. Calif says Claude Mythos Preview helped it break Apple’s M5 shield in five days. iOS 27.2 shipped 163 fixes: Anthropic Research credited on three, OpenAI on four.

Seven cases. About ten minutes each. The first takes ten seconds: update your iPhone.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ được tính theo công thức lũy thừa cơ bản:

$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (\text{với } n \neq -1)$$

Áp dụng với $n = 2$:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Kết luận:** 
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ là **$\dfrac{x^3}{3} + C$** (trong đó $C$ là hằng số tích phân).

items.title: The impossible standard we're setting for artificial intelligence | The Jerusalem Post
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence.

Artificial intelligence. (credit: SHUTTERSTOCK)

Others fear that increasingly autonomous AI will eventually become impossible to control. These concerns deserve serious attention, particularly as AI agents gain access to financial systems, corporate networks, sensitive information, and critical infrastructure. [...] Until recently, AI was largely an assistant; we asked it questions, evaluated its responses, and decided what to do with the information. Increasingly, we are asking AI to carry out the work directly.

An agent can be given an objective, determine the steps required, and execute them with limited human involvement. This transition has understandably generated anxiety as people worry about losing their jobs to systems that can perform tasks faster and more cheaply than they can. [...] Updated:

Four years ago, most people had never held a conversation with an AI system. Today, millions routinely turn to ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for everything from writing software to making financial decisions.

In that short period, we have witnessed a remarkable technological transformation, and I believe the most consequential stage is only beginning. The emergence of autonomous AI agents represents a fundamental change in our relationship with machines.

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
